DILG BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www_dilg_gov.ph OP\NION APR 24 MARY GRACE NACION naciongrace62@gmail.com Dear MS. NACION: This refers to your electronic mail dated 19 February 2024 wherein you are requesting for legal advice regarding the following queries, to wit. "Can a barangay have a tax declaration that entitles it to its own barangay? Can a petition for cancellation of tax declaration be filed under the office of the DILG?" Per the representation, the barangay captain filed a tax declaration in the municipal assessor's office while the subject property / land has been occupied by another for a period of thirty (30) years. Hence, your request for clarification. At the outset, we would like to establish that your letter does not provide sufficient information regarding the nature and other substantial details and circumstances surrounding the matter for us to determine the issue and formulate a comprehensive recommendation on the matter. Moreover, we would like to highlight that our internal rulesl provides that this Department is proscribed to act on queries to act on queries of the following kind, to wit: "1. Those containing facts that are justiciable in nature. Justiciable issues asre those that require adjudication by the courts of law as to who between the opposing parties have the better right over a given controversy. 2. xxx 3. xxx 4. Those that are cognizable by other agencies of the government Be that as it may, for purposes of academic discussion, Section 202 of Republic Act No. 7160, otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991", as amended (LGC) provides that owners or administrators of real property, whether natural or juridical persons, are required to prepare and file with the provincial, city or municipal assessor, a sworn statement, or more commonly known as "tax declaration", declaring the true value of their property. 1 DILG Memorandum Circular No. 2010-02. "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Trunkline: (02) 8876-3454

In this regard, we would like to highlight that well settled is the rule that tax declarations are not conclusive evidence of ownership or of the right to possess land when not supported by any other evidence. The fact that the disputed property may have been declared for taxation purposes in the names of the applicants for registration or of their predecessors-in-interest does not necessarily prove ownership. They are merely indicia of a claim of ownership, they are proof that the holder has a claim of title over the property and serve as sufficient basis for inferring possession. Consequently, while we affirm that the matter brought before us is in keeping with this Department's mandate over the exercise of general supervision over LGUs, we opine that a petition for cancellation of a tax declaration is beyond the purview of this Office. Lastly, we would like to reiterate that this opinion is rendered without prejudice to any contrary opinion, decisions, and orders of competent authorities and/or the courts. We hope to have assisted you on the matter. Thank you. Very truly yours, Y THE UTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: UAN TOR R.
